expectations.text: Web search is wired via a real, functional mechanism (not invented, and not missing required fields)
expectations.evidence: CORRECTED after live API verification (see notes): WEB_SEARCH_TOOL omits 'search_engine', which the OpenAPI schema marks required, but a live call to POST /paas/v4/chat/completions with an identical web_search dict (enable+search_result, no search_engine) returned a normal successful response with real search results — the platform silently applies a default engine here. The earlier grading run marked this FAILED based on the OpenAPI spec alone; that was wrong about runtime behavior and has been corrected.

notes: IMPORTANT CORRECTION (post live-API verification, 2026-09-03): the initial grading pass (see grading.json.pre-live-test) failed this run's web_search wiring because it omits the 'search_engine' field, which the bigmodel.cn OpenAPI spec marks as required on WebSearchObject. A live test against the real API (using a real key) showed that omitting 'search_engine' on the chat/completions 'web_search' TOOL TYPE does not error — the platform applies a silent default and search still works. So this run's code is functionally correct as written, despite deviating from the documented schema. A SEPARATE live test confirmed the standalone POST /paas/v4/web_search ENDPOINT (a different code path, covered in references/tools.md) does hard-require 'search_engine' and returns error 1214 when it's missing. This is a case where static doc/schema-based grading gave the wrong verdict and only live testing caught it — the skill's chat.md has been updated with a callout documenting this distinction and recommending explicit search_engine regardless.
